summary: Minimal and honest: a one-value config flip with a doctrine comment, a one-tuple-entry freeze extension that inherits writer/checker agreement from the shared GATE_FILES constant, and test coverage that proves the full lifecycle — init ships the default, upgrade restores it after a client reverts it, drift on hooks.json is named, adopt repairs a disarmed legacy hook. The delegation-behavior caveat (workers already ran workspace-write) is recorded in decision 0041 rather than papered over. The .codex write block the sandbox itself imposed was resolved through the ledgered degraded window, not worked around.

non_blocking_findings.summary: Only hooks.json joins the frozen surface; explore.config.toml and .codex/agents/*.toml remain unfrozen — acceptable (they are role configs, not gates), noted so the boundary is a choice, not an accident.

residual_risks: Escape-hatch enforcement is visibility-not-prevention by design (decision 0041, same ceiling as 0030).

contract_verdicts.evidence: .codex/config.toml:15-18 — sandbox_mode = "workspace-write" with the three-line escape-hatch comment naming decision 0041 and upgrade restoration; test_gates.py:2593-2594 asserts it post-init and :2627 post-upgrade after a simulated client revert to danger-full-access.

check_vendor_integrity.py:24 adds .codex/hooks.json to GATE_FILES — a shared constant consumed by both the checker (:43) and write_manifest, so all writers agree by construction; drift named at test_gates.py:12397, adopt repair of a disarmed legacy hook at :12636-12651.

config.toml is absent from GATE_FILES/GATE_TREES (check_vendor_integrity.py:23-24) — deliberately unhashed; docs/decisions/0041-sandboxed-workers-default.md records the flip, the escape-hatch doctrine, the visibility-not-prevention ceiling, and states plainly that delegation already ran workspace-write. Acceptance of 0041 remains the human's.

This story's own SBX-T1 delegation ran under the companion's workspace-write mapping end to end — including proving the sandbox live when it refused the worker's .codex write (signal S-0001-5481), resolved via degraded window Q-0058-38ee; recorded in the automated testing artifact.
